Multi-frequency ultra wide bandwidth transducer

Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (pMUT) arrays and techniques for frequency shaping in pMUT arrays are described, for example to achieve both high frequency and low frequency operation in a same device. The ability to

operate at both high and low frequencies may be tuned during use of the device to adaptively adjust for optimal resolution at a particular penetration depth of interest. In embodiments, various sizes of piezoelectric membranes are

fabricated for tuning resonance frequency across the membranes. The variously sized piezoelectric membranes are lumped together by two or more separate electrode rails, enabling independent addressing between the two or more subgroups of

sized transducer elements. Signal processing of the drive and/or response signals generated and/or received from each of the two or more electrode rails may achieve a variety of operative modes for the device, such as a near field mode, a
far field mode, and an ultra wide bandwidth mode.

source_evidence_quotes.text: Piezoelectric element and its manufacturing method

<P>PROBLEM TO BE SOLVED: To provide a method of manufacturing a piezoelectric element which can prevent faults by internal defects and holes.  <P>SOLUTION: Fine particles, each of which is a raw material for the piezoelectric

element, are sintered to make an ingot consiting of a fine particle sintered body. Then, the ingot is sliced into a plate-like piezoelectric body 206, which is then ground and thinned into a piezoelectric plate. The piezoelectric plate is

divided into piezoelectric elements. When sintering the fine particles, a cavity 210 remains and will become an internal defect or hole of the piezoelectric element. In order to avoid this, the sliced plate-like piezoelectric body 206 is

dipped in an insulating liquid 304. Since the plate-like piezoelectric body 206 is a fine particle sintered body, the insulating liquid 304 permeates along the grain boundaries of the fine particles 202 (304A) and thereby the cavity 210 is

filled with the insulating liquid 304 (304B). Then, the plate-like piezoelectric body 206 with its cavity 210 now filled up with the insulating liquid 304 is taken out of the insulating liquid 304 and is heated to solidify the insulating

liquid 304. Thus, the internal defect or hole of the piezoelectric element is filled up with the insulating liquid 304, preventing a decline in piezoelectric characteristics of the piezoelectric element.  <P>COPYRIGHT:

source_evidence_quotes.text: Ion beam flow marking method and device therefor

PURPOSE:To obviate the feed of ions by feeding air to realize a small-size and simple-structure device by a method wherein liquid fluid is heated to vaporize and expand, and the generated ions are jetted out of an ion discharge port.

CONSTITUTION:In a chamber 16 provided with a supply port 12 for liquid fluid 10 and ion discharge ports 14, a main part of a device consists of a thermal vaporization means 20 for vaporizing and expanding the liquid fluid 10, a liquid

supply means 22 for supplying the liquid fluid to the thermal vaporization means 20, and an ion generation means 30 for ionizing a gas in the chamber 16. When a voltage is applied to an arbitrary heating resistor 20 in accordance with

image information and a high tension voltage is applied to a corotron wire 30, the liquid fluid 10 is dripped on the heating resistor 20 and simultaneously expanded. A bubble generated by the vaporization and expansion moves toward the ion

discharge port 14 together with ions generated by the corotron wire 30, thus resulting in an ion beam being jetted to an image holding body 40 as shown by an arrow A. In this manner, the need for a force feed means, such as a blower, is
eliminated, and the device can be reduced in size and simplified in structure as a whole.
